questions.stem: Why might the actual ratio of offspring phenotypes differ from the expected ratio predicted by a Punnett square?

options.text: Because Punnett squares are always incorrect
Because fertilisation is a random process and predicted ratios are only probabilities
Because dominant alleles are stronger than recessive ones
Because parents always pass on the same alleles

questions.explanation: Punnett squares show the probability of each outcome. The actual results may differ because fertilisation involves chance, and larger sample sizes are needed to see ratios closer to the predicted ones.
